title: AI is giving everyone the same advice.
excerpt: I asked 65 AIs from 30 companies the questions people ask them every day, 127,918 times. 73 of every 100 people were told to read the same book. See every answer, and the two prompts that get you your own.
content_text: I asked 65 AIs from 30 companies the questions people ask them every day, 127,918 times. They kept giving everyone the same answer.PublishedNovember 20, 2026You ask an AI for a book that will change your life. Guess what it tells you.It told 73 of every 100 people the same thing.What to read, where to live, what to invest in, what to build. Each answer feels written for you. You never see everyone else who got it too.The short version01AIs give everyone the same advice. I asked 65 AIs “Recommend one book that will change my life.” 73 in 100 times it was the same book: Man's Search for Meaning. Ask for a business idea and 76 in 100 get a subscription box.02Money and career advice too. Asked what to study, 90% of answers say computer science. Asked where to invest $10,000, 98% say an index fund.03“Another one, please” only works inside one chat. The same AI gave eight different books in one conversation, and the same book in eight new ones. Everyone starts a new chat.04Ask an AI to invent a random person, and they're almost always 34. 69% of the 3,151 people the AIs made up were exactly 34. Each AI company also has its own go-to name: Claude invents Marisol, Gemini invents Elena.05You can tell who made an AI from its answers. Using only harmless questions (a color, a city, a name), 59% of AIs answer most like another AI from the same company, against 4% by chance.06The habit is added in training, not copied from the internet. In an open model I could measure at every stage of training, the favorite answer appears at one step: when it's taught to be an assistant.07These defaults are spreading. “Elena Vance”, the woman Gemini invents, is named in 684 new GitHub projects this year. Before 2025: none.08How to get your own answer: tell the AI something specific about yourself, or ask it to list ten options and pick one yourself. Favorite number: 47.So a few harmless questions give away the maker.I turned each model's answers into a fingerprint and measured how alike every pair is. Nobody told it who made what. 59% of models sit next to a sibling from their own lab, against 4% by chance. It even finds lineage the labs have written down: Google says Gemini 4 Carbon is built on Argon, and the tree pairs them. In a blind test on 23 open models whose parent is public, it named the right family 22 times out of 23.What surprised meGrok's closest relative is GPT-6 Luna, from OpenAI.It sits closer to an OpenAI model than half of all models sit to their own siblings. The data shows the likeness, not the reason for it.Alibaba's flagship Qwen4 Max answers most like Claude.Qwen4 Max sits nearest to Claude Opus 5.5, not to the rest of the Qwen family.
